title: Mitigating the Negative Consequences of Work Stressors: The Role of Perceived Meaning and Calling
abstract: The purpose of the present study was to understand how meaningful work and vocational calling may benefit employees’ work and well-being under circumstances of job stressors. Drawing on the Job Demands-Resources framework, we tested a model linking stressor exposure to work and health outcomes through one’s experience of meaningful work, and dependent on one’s perception of work calling via a two time-point survey of 493 employees. Exposure to particular stressors and evaluated workplace and health-relevant outcomes were consistently linked, and further support was found for the role of calling in buffering the impact of certain stressors on outcomes through work meaning. This study contributes to the occupational health and career development literatures by expanding our understanding of detriments to job-related (i.e., job satisfaction and turnover intentions) and well-being-related (i.e., physical symptoms and burnout) criterion variables from workplace stressors. Implications for organizations and counselors, study limitations, and future directions are discussed.
